measurement: One visit examines an ordered pair of captured left and right row occurrences for correlation, direction or tolerance eligibility. Count rejected pairs as well as eligible candidates. Re-examination counts again. Equal values, repeated targets and repeated authored by fields do not merge occurrence pairs; evaluation within one visit remains separately budgeted physical work.
fallback: Use L * R from applicable nonnegative safe-integer operand row bounds only for a selected realization that examines each ordered occurrence pair at most once. This rule is independent of left or inner output kind and backward, forward or nearest direction. The left-preserving output bound is not a search bound. A known zero operand gives zero pair visits even when the other bound is unknown; unknown is not zero.
arithmetic: Validate every supplied operand bound, then multiply exactly. Reject overflow beyond 9007199254740991 without rounding or saturation. Missing or overflowing product evidence leaves this fallback unavailable, not the language invalid; another admitted finite bound may apply with its own conditions. Without an applicable finite bound search resolution is incomplete.
ownership: Retain the exact checked as-of operation, both ordered operand occurrences, effective Parameter binding, original producer contexts and all applicable operand-bound dependencies. Foreign proofs, equal numeric values, output limits and observations do not substitute for these associations.
enforcement: Select the finite ceiling before matching. Permit equality and fail atomically on the next pair visit without exposing partial successful output. A strategy revisiting pairs must account for those visits under another admitted bound; it cannot claim this fallback. Choosing a strategy is not proof that execution satisfied it.
separation: Validate both inputs' clocks and all required identities even with zero pair visits or no match. Checked distance arithmetic, best-candidate and tie comparison, sorting or indexing, received bytes, retained candidates and output allocation retain their own validation and physical resource budgets. These costs are not bounded by pair_visits. This contract neither requires materializing candidate arrays nor permits changing nearest ties, tie-break completion, output order or failure rules.
authority: This is a search-measurement and applicability contract, not a row-count law, backend conformance attestation, observed count or execution permit. It adds no authored option, hidden default or implicit truncation. It does not replace output-capacity or complete-input validation requirements. Interval and as-of search contracts have distinct identities despite sharing product arithmetic.
